legend: Invasive, keratinizing, well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in association with carcinoma in situ is shown. The adjacent substantia propria demonstrates severe actinic elastosis, compatible with a sun-exposed location.

diagnosis: Conjunctival well-differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma
legend: Higher magnification showing atypical squamous cells with squamous eddy and keratin pearl formation.

diagnosis: Conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma with mucinous differentiation
legend: Bands and strands of invasive squamous cell carcinoma with focal keratin pearl formation (upper left) and bluish mucin within individual tumour cells (lower right).

diagnosis: Conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma with mucinous differentiation
legend: Higher magnification of the signet ring–like or goblet cell–like cells containing cytoplasmic mucin.

diagnosis: Conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma with mucinous differentiation
legend: Alcian blue stain highlighting intracytoplasmic mucin in some of the tumour cells.
A high-power view shows basaloid poorly differentiated invasive squamous cell carcinoma. Note that the basaloid cells have a high N:C ratio and do not show keratinization.

A This keratotic nodule showed invasive SCC histologically. B The tumour has pushing, rather than infiltrative, deep borders; determining the degree of dysplasia and differentiating in situ from invasive disease can be clinically challenging. C The index of clinical suspicion for SCC is higher in larger lesions such as this one. D Histologically, this tumour has infiltrating borders. E,F Both in situ and invasive SCCs can occasionally involve pterygia.

legend: Sagittal T2-weighted MRI shows a mass in the left lower eyelid, of intermediate signal intensity on T2-weighted images and enhancing. Anteriorly, it is located posterior to both the inferior tarsus and the orbicularis oculi muscle. Posteriorly, there is orbital invasion, with the tumour extending until the region of the globe attachment of the inferior rectus muscle.
